_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1253's CONTRACT IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
tools/experiment-harness/replay-kit.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. Rebuilding the store a kit's record says it built is
a VERB, and it holds two refusals that have no flag: every file a step
feeds must be identical in the pinned tree and the tree today, and a step
the record marks `reject` must actually be rolled back. Take either away
and `replay-kit` still prints a digest — a digest that means something
else, which is the whole failure being guarded against.
THE OTHER TWO BREAK THE VOCABULARY. `expect` is the ONE field separating a
negative control from an import, and the verb-to-flag map is what turns a
step into a command; a fallback in either is a record read as something it
does not say.
WHAT THIS SWEEP DOES NOT COVER, said rather than left implied: that the
whole tracked corpus still rebuilds through the verb. That is
`every_replay_rebuilds_the_store_its_record_says_it_does`, which extracts
and compiles one workspace per declared revision — 205 seconds warm, and
an injection sweep over it would be four of those. It was run whole for
R1253 instead: 49 replays reproduced their declared digest, 2 blocked as
declared, 65 transcripts regenerated.

injections.name: a-replay-may-read-a-later-edit-of-its-own-input
injections.why: the failure R883 found in its own corpus: the record's inputs are read from the tree TODAY, so a replay whose input has been edited since reports the edit's result under the original's name. With the comparison gone the replay still succeeds and still prints a digest — of a different run

injections.name: a-negative-control-may-apply
injections.why: the record's `reject` steps are its probes. A replay in which they land has built a different store from the same inputs and has stopped controlling for anything — and it looks exactly like a replay that worked, because every other step did

injections.name: an-unreadable-expectation-becomes-the-permissive-one
injections.why: `expect` is the only field distinguishing a negative control from an import, so a fallback arm turns a typo into a step that is allowed to succeed. The record still reads as though it declares a probe

edits.from:
other => Err(format!(
                "a step expects `{other}`, and a record can only say `apply` or \
                 `reject` — a word nothing reads is a negative control nothing runs"
            )),

injections.name: a-verb-with-no-known-flag-is-guessed
injections.why: the map is what turns a declared step into a command. Guessing a flag hands the binary an argument it does not take, and what a reader then sees is the VERB complaining — a finding about the record, produced by this tool's own gap

edits.from:
other => Err(format!(
            "no input flag is known for the verb `{other}` — a replay cannot be \
             run against a verb this tool cannot address"
        )),
